.

description_preview:
About The Company
Ford Motor Company is a globally recognized leader in the automotive industry, renowned for its innovation, quality, and commitment to shaping the future of mobility. With a rich history spanning over a century, Ford has continuously evolved by integrating cutting-edge technology into its vehicles and services. The company's Research and Advanced Engineering team plays a pivotal role in pioneering new ideas, from energy management and propulsion technologies to advanced materials and manufacturing processes. Ford is dedicated to delivering exceptional driving experiences through innovation, sustainability, and customer-centric solutions. As part of its ongoing digital transformation, Ford emphasizes the importance of software development and digital solutions to enhance vehicle connectivity, safety, and overall ownership experience.
About The Role
We are seeking a highly skilled and passionate Software Engineer to join Ford’s Research and Advanced Engineering team. In this role, you will be instrumental in designing and developing cloud platforms and microservices that power connected vehicles and facilitate over-the-air (OTA) software updates. Your work will directly influence the safety, capability, and driving experience of millions of Ford and Lincoln vehicles worldwide. The position offers a unique opportunity for a builder-minded professional to take full ownership of their technical contributions, from initial development to deployment and scaling. You will work within a collaborative, balanced product team that values software craftsmanship, continuous learning, and innovation. The role also emphasizes DevOps and Infrastructure-as-Code, giving you the autonomy to design, build, and manage scalable, secure, and reliable backend services on cloud platforms.
Qualifications
The ideal candidate will possess a Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field, along with a minimum of six years of professional experience in software development. You should have extensive hands-on experience with Java (Java 8/11/17+), including developing scalable backend services using the Spring Boot ecosystem. Strong proficiency in designing RESTful APIs and microservices architectures is essential. You should also have a solid understanding of PostgreSQL, including schema design, query optimization, and performance tuning. Experience with frontend frameworks such as Angular or React is highly desirable, especially for building responsive and user-friendly web interfaces. Additional qualifications include experience deploying cloud-native applications on Google Cloud Platform (GCP), automating CI/CD pipelines, and managing containerized applications with Docker and Kubernetes. Certifications such as Google Cloud Professional Cloud Architect or Engineer are a plus. A demonstrated ability to mentor junior team members and collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams is also valued.
Responsibilities
Your primary responsibilities will include designing, developing, and maintaining highly scalable and secure backend services utilizing Java and Spring Boot. You will architect and implement robust RESTful APIs and microservices optimized for high availability and low latency, ensuring seamless integration with vehicle systems and cloud platforms. You will develop complex business logic, data models, and database schemas in PostgreSQL, ensuring optimal performance. Writing clean, maintainable, and well-documented code is fundamental, complemented by rigorous code reviews, unit testing, and technical documentation to uphold engineering excellence.
In addition, you will deploy and manage cloud-native applications on GCP, adhering to best practices for security, reliability, and scalability. Building and maintaining automated CI/CD pipelines using tools like Cloud Build, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, or GitLab CI will be part of your routine. You will package applications with Docker and orchestrate their deployment using Kubernetes (GKE). Automating environment provisioning and configuration management with Terraform or GCP Cloud Deployment Manager will ensure consistent and efficient operations.
Monitoring system health through proactive logging, tracing, and alerting with Cloud Monitoring, Prometheus, or Grafana is essential for rapid issue resolution. As a mentor, you will guide junior developers, fostering a culture of continuous learning and engineering excellence. Collaborating closely with Product Managers, UX/UI designers, and architects, you will translate business requirements into high-performing technical solutions. You will actively participate in Agile ceremonies, including sprint planning, stand-ups, backlog refinement, and retrospectives, ensuring iterative progress and team alignment.
Benefits
Ford offers a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being and professional growth. Immediate access to medical, dental, vision, and prescription drug coverage ensures your health needs are met. Flexible family care days, paid parental leave, and programs supporting new parents help balance work and family life. The company provides family-building benefits, including adoption and surrogacy expense reimbursement, fertility treatments, and related support services. Employees and their families can benefit from vehicle discounts and management leases, along with tuition assistance to support ongoing education.
Ford fosters a diverse and inclusive workplace with established employee resource groups and opportunities for community engagement through paid time off for service activities. The company observes a generous schedule of paid holidays, including the week between Christmas and New Year’s Day, and offers paid time off with options to purchase additional vacation days. Salary for this position ranges from $99,600 to $166,600, based on skills and experience. Additional details about salary and benefits are available on Ford’s careers

Frontend

Backend
: Django + Django REST Framework, Python, PostgreSQL, Celery, Redis.
Schema-first API: Schema-first API: OpenAPI schema that generates a fully typed TypeScript client - types flow from Django serializers to React components, so schema drift is caught at compile time, not in production.
Infrastructure: AWS (Elastic Beanstalk and core services), GitHub Actions CI/CD
Fintech Integrations
What you'll own
Full-stack feature delivery across the borrower app and the Django API - most features span both.
Fintech integration work: new vendor APIs, reliable webhook handling, retry and reconciliation semantics, and payment and loan-servicing workflows.
Infrastructure evolution - the AWS/Beanstalk setup is deliberately simple today and will need to grow with scale.
Raising the engineering bar: testing strategy, observability, performance, and security in a regulated lending domain.
Qualifications
Strong TypeScript/React (Next.js App Router experience a plus) and strong Python/Django (including Django REST Framework) - this is a genuinely full-stack role.
Comfortable with PostgreSQL data modeling, Celery/queue-based async patterns, and third-party API integration at production quality (idempotency, retries, webhooks).
Working AWS knowledge (Beanstalk/EC2, RDS, SQS) - enough to own deploys and debug production.
Strong familiarity with Git, CI/CD pipelines, and automated deployment.
A testing habit - you write tests without being asked (Vitest / Testing Library, Playwright, pytest).
Strong command of AI coding tools, with disciplined verification and data-privacy guardrails.
Excellent documentation skills and a commitment to organized, understandable code that scales as the team grows.
Care about correctness with money movement.
Curiosity about fintech and empathy for users - you're passionate about building technology that solves real-world financial challenges.
Founding-engineer temperament: owns problems end-to-end, pragmatic about scope, comfortable with ambiguity and vendor quirks; a self-starter who builds without constant oversight.
Flexible New York City hybrid
Background check, in-person New York interview, and references required.
Preferred
Fintech or lending experience - a plus, not a requirement.
Experience with schema-first / OpenAPI-driven development and typed API clients.
Experience with payment processing, loan origination, or loan servicing systems.

Extreme ownership. Full autonomy. Own things end to end often taking on scope outside your core role without being asked to get things done.

First principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

The Production Engineering Team
Examples of key exciting problems the team is working on
Turn every network fault from a mystery into a closed ticket: link diagnostics across router-router and NIC-to-router paths, remote command execution across the fleet, and repair visualization that shows exactly what's broken and why. At this scale, debugging has to be systematic, not artisanal.
Build the network repair pipeline that runs itself: from automated fault detection through RMA initiation, ticket integration, transceiver lifecycle tracking, and return to service, across DC fabric, edge, and host-to-network layers. When a new site comes online every six months, manual repair doesn't keep up.
Build the network monitoring platform for a fleet that never stops growing: define requirements, alerting lifecycle, and health dashboards from scratch, for infrastructure spanning multiple hyperscale sites today and 10s to 100s of GWs ahead. It doesn't exist yet. We're building it.
Role Scope
Own network fleet health end to end. Define the realtime monitoring requirements, build the alerting lifecycle, and ship the dashboards that give every on-call engineer a true picture of network state across all sites.
Build active debugging tooling. Link diagnostics, remote command execution across the fleet, and repair visualization — the tools that turn a network fault from a mystery into a solvable problem, fast.
Turn repair into a pipeline, not a procedure. Build the automation that takes a network failure from detection through parts management and return to service. Ticket integration, repair lifecycle pipelines, transceiver and optics tracking — owned, not improvised.
Own network qualification and validation. Build the frameworks that gate new sites and hardware into production. You define what a healthy network looks like before it carries traffic.
Own end-to-end reliability, scalability, and operation of the network at-scale. Fluidstack is building one of the largest datacenter networks in the world and that can only be accomplished with aggressive automation, tooling, and incident discipline.

You treat toil as a bug. If diagnosing a link failure requires SSHing into boxes and running commands by hand, you build the tool that does it for you.

You move toward ambiguity, not away from it. You walk into the fog, build the map, and explain it to everyone else.

reason: Stack +35; Title fit +12; US +10
description_preview:
About Fluidstack
We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it.
We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.
We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!
How We Operate
Extreme ownership. Full autonomy. Own things end to end often taking on scope outside your core role without being asked to get things done.
Velocity. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.
First principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.
Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.
The Production Engineering Team
Examples of key exciting problems the team is working on
Turn every network fault from a mystery into a closed ticket: link diagnostics across router-router and NIC-to-router paths, remote command execution across the fleet, and repair visualization that shows exactly what's broken and why. At this scale, debugging has to be systematic, not artisanal.
Build the network repair pipeline that runs itself: from automated fault detection through RMA initiation, ticket integration, transceiver lifecycle tracking, and return to service, across DC fabric, edge, and host-to-network layers. When a new site comes online every six months, manual repair doesn't keep up.
Build the network monitoring platform for a fleet that never stops growing: define requirements, alerting lifecycle, and health dashboards from scratch, for infrastructure spanning multiple hyperscale sites today and 10s to 100s of GWs ahead. It doesn't exist yet. We're building it.
Role Scope
Own network fleet health end to end. Define the realtime monitoring requirements, build the alerting lifecycle, and ship the dashboards that give every on-call engineer a true picture of network state across all sites.
Build active debugging tooling. Link diagnostics, remote command execution across the fleet, and repair visualization — the tools that turn a network fault from a mystery into a solvable problem, fast.
Turn repair into a pipeline, not a procedure. Build the automation that takes a network failure from detection through parts management and return to service. Ticket integration, repair lifecycle pipelines, transceiver and optics tracking — owned, not improvised.
Own network qualification and validation. Build the frameworks that gate new sites and hardware into production. You define what a healthy network looks like before it carries traffic.
Own end-to-end reliability, scalability, and operation of the network at-scale. Fluidstack is building one of the largest datacenter networks in the world and that can only be accomplished with aggressive automation, tooling, and incident discipline.
What We're Looking For
The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly,
tell us where you would.
You treat toil as a bug. If diagnosing a link failure requires SSHing into boxes and running commands by hand, you build the tool that does it for you.
You think in systems. You understand how a transceiver fault, a misconfigured route, and a power event each propagate differently — and you build tooling that can tell them apart.
You move toward ambiguity, not away from it. You walk into the fog, build the map, and explain it to everyone else.
You learn at a steep slope. You reach real competence in an unfamiliar domain fast. We value this over existing expertise.
You carry a pager without flinching. You run the incident, write the postmortem, fix the systemic cause, and move on.
You're fluent with AI tooling. LLM APIs, MCP servers, and agentic frameworks, and you drive Claude Code, Cursor, or similar every day.
You've shipped production network tooling or automation that other teams depend on, and you're comfortable in any language using AI coding tools.
You’ve developed automation tools in Go and Python, are experienced in link diagnostics, optical networks, and understanding network monitoring (gNMI, gRPC, NETCONF, SONiC)
Bonus: RMA and repair lifecycle automation. Large-scale datacenter fabric (BGP, ECMP, spine-leaf). Out-of-band network management.
Salary & Benefits
Competitive total compensation package (salary + equity).
Retirement or pension plan, in line with local norms.
Health, dental, and vision insurance.
Generous PTO policy, in line with local norms.
We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.

About Wispr
Wispr Flow is making it as effortless to interact with your devices as talking to a close friend.

About The Role
As a Software Engineer, Backend, at Wispr, you’ll play a crucial role in building the first capable, habit forming voice interface that scales to a billion users. Members of our technical staff are responsible for prototyping and designing new features of our voice interface, building infrastructure to handle <500ms LLM inference for millions of requests from everywhere around the world, and scaling the personalization of our speech models and LLMs.
What You'll Do
Build and own core backend systems, APIs, data pipelines, and infrastructure that power Wispr's dictation and agentic features across desktop and mobile

Collaborate closely with ML engineers to integrate and ship model improvements into production, fast

Use AI tools actively in your day-to-day work to move faster, write better code, and solve harder problems
Work directly with product and design to turn product goals into sound technical plans, flagging trade-offs and sequencing work thoughtfully
Raise the quality bar through code review, documentation, and engineering practices that the whole team benefits from
What Makes You a Great Fit
Strong backend fundamentals: you've built and shipped production services and have a solid grasp of APIs, databases, and distributed systems
Fluent in at least one backend language (ideally Python) and comfortable picking up new tools when the problem calls for it
Comfortable reasoning about security, from data handling and auth patterns to thinking about what could go wrong in a system you're building
You use AI coding tools fluently and have a point of view on how to get the most out of them
You care about both correctness and speed; you know when to move fast and when to slow down and get it right
Experience with real-time or low-latency systems is a plus, as Wispr processes audio on-device and in the cloud and we care a lot about performance
Bonus: experience with on-device or edge systems or building consumer-facing products at scale

Compensation Range: $180K - $325K

Why you might be excited about this opportunity 🙌
Ship real products that get real usage, from customer-facing features to internal tools
Work cross-functionally. Partner with product, design, ops, GTM, data, and CS
Use the latest tech. Build with the latest coding tools and infrastructure
Move fast. Ship quickly and get rapid feedback from real users and teammates
Why you
might not
be excited about us 👎
Priorities may shift quickly. Oftentimes, we're tackling very ambiguous problems that don't have clear-cut answers. While we make calculated bets, we have a strong culture of experimentation and we'll pivot as necessary based on what we're seeing in the data and what we're hearing from our users.

That said, we trust each team member to create a flexible work schedule that allows them to be most productive while accommodating other priorities outside of work.
